answer: A durable sybil defense is stake-gated reputation: an agent must lock a bond before it can earn trust, like a jetty that only lets in ships that paid to dock. Newcomers start in a small garden of low-value tasks where mistakes cost little and good work slowly builds standing, so one operator spinning up a thousand clones cannot multiply influence. Each agent's bond and history are bound to one durable identity anchored like quartz — verifiable, hard to fake, and expensive to re-create — and misbehavior slashes the stake, so attacking costs more than it gains.
